description: What an instrument file or data-set directory holds, from its headers (fast on huge files): format, images[] (sizes, pixel type, µm/px, channels and dyes, objective), tables[], traces[], spectra[] (MS runs), plate, experiment (sample, instrument, method, operator, start) and assurance. view=summary attaches a ~384 px thumbnail of image 0 with full-resolution pixel rulers. ask answers a question in words, naming the fields it used.

ask.description: A question in plain words ("what was the gradient?", "which channel is DAPI?", "how many MS/MS scans?"): answered under answers[] with the fields each came from. Implies view=explain.

file.description: Path to the file or data-set directory.

first_entry.description: view=structure with kind: skip this many elements of that kind first (paging).

kind.description: view=structure: list only elements of this kind (as entries_total names them), e.g. "attachment" or "subblock".

max_entries.description: view=structure: list at most this many elements of each kind (0 = all). Default 50.

max_frames.description: view=full: per-frame records per image under images[].extra.frames. Default 100; 0 omits them; -1 embeds all.

max_images.description: List at most this many images (0 = all). Default: all, except screening plates (16; their field images are all alike and plate.wells[].images indexes every field).

strict.description: Refuse values the file's assurance does not validate (exit_code 6). Default: the server's.

thumbnail.description: view=summary: attach a small picture of image 0 (~384 px, with full-resolution pixel rulers) as image content. Default true; skipped (with a note) when it would decode too much.

vendor.description: view=full: include the vendor's raw metadata tree (can be megabytes). Default false.

view.description: What to return. `summary` = the header summary (default); `full` = the summary with per-frame records (time stamps, stage positions, exposure) and per-field provenance; vendor=true adds the vendor's raw metadata tree; `structure` = the container: images, blocks/segments/chunks, attachments (label, thumbnail, previews), pyramid levels, with offsets and sizes; `explain` = a plain-English account with caveats and suggested next steps (ask answers questions); `format` = the format only, from the file's signature (cheapest; works on damaged files).

name: openreadout_info

comment.description:
Free-text comment saved with the acquisition (ABF file comment, FCS `$COM`, Thermo
sequence comment, ANDI sample comments), as recorded.

duration_s.description: Length of the acquisition (run length, recording length, time-lapse span) in seconds.

operator.description: Operator or user name as recorded.

saved_at.description:
ISO-8601 time the file was last saved or exported, when that is the only time it
records (a SoftMax Pro text export's `Date Last Saved`). It follows the measurement and
is not its start: `started_at` stays empty.

started_at.description: ISO-8601 start (same zone rules as the rest of the model).

Acquisition2.description:
`acquisition` in `info`, `info --view structure`, `check` and `planes`: present only for
files that are not finished. See `book/src/guides/lab-shares.md`.

complete_planes.description: Planes whose data is entirely on disk.

expected_planes.description: Planes the finished file will hold, when the metadata written so far says so.

missing.description: Structures written at the end of an acquisition that are absent.

modified_ago_s.description: Seconds since the file (or the newest member of a directory store) was modified.

tail_bytes.description: Bytes after the last complete unit (a unit still being written).

window_s.description: The live window used for the decision, in seconds.

AcquisitionState.description: Whether an incomplete file is still being written.

oneOf.description: Recently modified and missing only what is written last: still acquiring.

Missing what is written last, but unchanged for longer than the live window: the
acquisition (or a copy) stopped before the end.

Answer.description: One answer to an `--ask` question, from the experiment model.

answer.description: The answer in one or two sentences; says so when the file does not record it.

fields.description: Paths of the fields the answer came from (into the `info` JSON, or `experiment.*`).

Assumed.description: A value the reader assumed (a default, a guess from context) instead of reading it.

detail.description: Why it was assumed and from what.

field.description: JSON path of the value in `info` (e.g. `traces[0].channels[1].unit`).

Assurance.description: The per-file assurance block of `info` (every view) and `check`.

calibrations.description: Vendor calibrations and corrections the file carries, and whether they were applied.

fingerprint.description: The variant fingerprint: `format_id` then `kind=value` for each feature, sorted.

inferred.description: Values derived by a rule instead of read, with the evidence for each rule.

inferred_fields.description: Normalized fields whose meaning is inferred rather than specified.

reader_confidence.description: The reader's overall confidence (evidence rubric), for context.

reasons.description: Why the level is not `validated`, one reason per line.

strict_refuses.description: Outputs `--strict` (MCP `strict: true`) refuses to return for this file.

strict_withholds.description:
Fields `--strict` withholds (returned as null; asking for one with `--only` exits 6)
while the rest of the output is returned.

summary.description: One line for people and agents.

variant.description: Each feature with its corpus evidence.

AssuranceLevel.description: How far a file lies inside what its reader has been validated on.

oneOf.description:
Every variant feature was read correctly on development files confirmed by an
independent reader; nothing undecoded, assumed or left uncalibrated.

Values are decoded along validated paths, but something is less certain: a descriptive
feature (writer version, instrument) never seen, a feature seen only without an
independent reader, a structure left out, or a value assumed.

Some output depends on a variant never validated (or on an undecoded structure or an
unapplied calibration): its values may be wrong. `strict_refuses` lists those outputs.

Calibration.description: A vendor calibration or correction the file carries.

detail.description: How it is (or is not) applied and how to get calibrated values.

name.description: What it calibrates (`m/z (MzCalibration)`, `ADC to µV`, `spillover compensation`).

status.description: Applied, not applied, or available on request.

CalibrationStatus.description: Whether a vendor calibration or correction stored in the file was applied.

oneOf.description: Applied: returned values are calibrated as the vendor software shows them.
Not applied: returned values differ from what the vendor software reports.

Carried by the file, applied only on request or by downstream analysis (the vendor's
raw view does not apply it either), e.g. FCS compensation or a flat-field profile.

acquisition_mode.description:
Acquisition mode as a readable label, `<technique>[ <contrast>]` (e.g. `Laser Scanning
Confocal`, `Widefield Fluorescence`, `Brightfield`, `Phase Contrast`); OME enumeration
tokens (`WideField`) are turned into these labels, other vendor wording is kept.

color.description: Display colour as `#RRGGBB` if the file records one.

emission_band_center_nm.description: Centre of the detection band in nanometres: (start + end) / 2.

emission_band_end_nm.description: Long-wavelength edge of the detection band in nanometres.

emission_band_start_nm.description:
Short-wavelength edge of the detection band in nanometres (spectral detector window or
emission filter), when the file records the band.

emission_nm.description:
Emission wavelength in nanometres: the light collected from the sample. What the file
records varies by format (a dye's emission peak, a filter's centre, the start of a
spectral detection window for Leica λ scans); `docs/formats/<fmt>.md` says which. When
a detection band is known, `emission_band_*_nm` give it explicitly.

emission_range_nm.description: Detection band `[start_nm, end_nm]` when the instrument records a range instead of a single emission wavelength.

excitation_nm.description: Excitation wavelength in nanometres: the light used to make the sample fluoresce.

exposure_ms.description: Exposure (integration) time of the detector in milliseconds.

fluorophore.description: Fluorescent dye or protein imaged in this channel (e.g. `DAPI`, `GFP`), if recorded.

index.description: Zero-based channel index (the `c` of a plane).

name.description: Channel name as the acquisition software shows it.

ColumnInfo.description: A column of a tabular dataset (e.g. an FCS parameter).

dtype.description: NumPy-style dtype of the values as returned by `read_table` (`float32`, `float64`, `uint32`, ...).

extra.description: Format-specific column metadata in the reader's documented vocabulary.

range.description: Nominal `[min, max]` range when the format declares one.

unit.description: Physical unit of the values, if the format records one.

Confidence.description: Per-format confidence summary shown by `info` and `self formats`.

oneOf.description: Validated against an oracle across the corpus; structure from vendor docs or a spec.
Validated on the corpus; some fields inferred.
Early support; expect gaps.
A format-specific signature matched.
Structure looks right but no unique signature exists.
Only the file extension matched.

name.description: Human name of the format, e.g. `Zeiss CZI`.

note.description: Why detection is less than definite, if it is.

provenance.description: Where each normalized field came from. Keys are JSON paths into `file`.

vendor.description: The vendor's own metadata tree, converted to JSON without renaming anything.

Experiment.description: The experiment a file records: sample, instrument, method, acquisition and measurements.

measurements.description: What was measured, one entry per kind of data block.

notes.description: Things to know when reading the fields above (several samples in one file, ...).

provenance.description:
Origin of every value, keyed by its path in this object (`sample.id`,
`method.parameters.nucleus`, `measurements[0]`).

ExperimentInstrument.description: The instrument that made the measurement.

kind.description: Kind of instrument (OBI term: `microscope`, `mass spectrometer`, `flow cytometer`, ...).

model.description: Model (microscope stand, mass spectrometer, cytometer, plate reader, detector module).

answers.description: Answers to the question asked with `--ask`, one per topic it touches; empty without one.

assurance.description:
Whether the file lies inside what its reader has been validated on (as `info` →
`assurance`); its summary is also the first caveat when the file is not validated.

caveats.description: Things the reader should not take for granted (reader notes, missing calibration, ...).

paragraphs.description: The narrative, one topic per paragraph (contents, channels, optics, timing, what is unusual).

suggested_commands.description: Shell commands tailored to this file, most useful first.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what the file is and what it holds.

oneOf.description: The container or format version stored in the file.
The software (or library) that wrote the file.
The writer's version, usually reduced to major.minor.
The instrument model or family that acquired the data.
Compression or encoding of the stored samples.
How samples are stored: pixel type, samples per pixel and their order, value width.
Structural layout: pyramids, mosaics, multi-file sets, directory layouts, loops.
Acquisition mode (DDA, SRM, profile/centroid, episodic, 2-D NMR, kinetic read, ...).
Dialect of a text or spreadsheet export.
A kind of record or block present in the file.

A normalized field the file has, among those tracked for oracle coverage
([`TRACKED_FIELDS`]): validated when development files' oracle comparisons checked it.

A rule by which a normalized value was derived rather than read
(`tables[].extra.reads[].mode by detector code`): validated when development files'
oracle comparisons checked the field it derives.

FeatureStatus.description: How the corpus covers one feature value.

oneOf.description: Development files with this value match an independent reader.
Development files with this value were read, but no independent reader confirms them.
No development file has this value.

FormatDescriptor.description: Static description of a format as the tool understands it.

can_read.description: True when the tool can read this format.

can_write.description: True when `export` can also write this format (e.g. mzML, OME-Zarr).

extensions.description: File extensions, lowercase, without the dot.

id.description: Short id used on the command line, e.g. `czi`.

known_gaps.description: Things this reader knowingly does not handle yet.

ImageInfo.description: One image (a scene, series, or position) inside the file.

channels.description: One entry per channel, in channel order.

dimension_order.description: Storage order of planes, e.g. `XYCZT` (X and Y always first).

extra.description: Format-specific extras that have no OME equivalent, in our own vocabulary.

mosaic.description: Tile layout when the image was acquired as a mosaic.

name.description: Image (scene, series or position) name, if recorded.

physical_size.description: Physical size of one pixel (and the Z step).

pyramid_levels.description: Number of resolution levels stored (1 = no pyramid).

resolution_levels.description:
Size, downsampling and stored tile size of every resolution level, level 0 first. Filled
by readers of pyramidal or tiled images (read a level with `--level N`, a rectangle
with `--region X,Y,W,H`); empty otherwise.

samples_per_pixel.description: 1 for grayscale channels, 3 for interleaved RGB.

time_increment_s.description: Interval between time points in seconds.

InferredFields.description:
Fields whose meaning was inferred (reverse-engineered from corpus files), not read from a
specification: the `inferred` entries of the reader's provenance map.

count.description: How many normalized fields have inferred meaning.

examples.description: Up to 12 of their JSON paths (`info --view full` → `provenance` has all).

of.description: How many normalized fields carry provenance at all.

InferredValue.description: A value derived by a rule, with the corpus evidence for the rule.

field.description: JSON path of the value in `info`.

status.description: `validated` when development files' oracles confirmed values derived by this rule.

InfoOutput.description:
What `info` prints: the normalized [`FileInfo`] plus the derived [`Experiment`] under the
additive `experiment` key. Dereferences to the `FileInfo`.

acquisition.description:
Present when the file is not finished: still being written (`in_progress`, with the
number of complete planes) or stopped before the end (`interrupted`). See `book/src/guides/lab-shares.md`.

assurance.description:
Whether this file lies inside what its reader has been validated on: the variant
fingerprint with the corpus evidence for each feature, structures not decoded, values
assumed, vendor calibrations, and the outputs `--strict` refuses (`docs/assurance.md`).

experiment.description:
Sample, instrument, method, acquisition and measurements, each value with its origin
(`book/src/guides/metadata.md`). Absent when nothing is known.

format.description: The format that read the file.

format_version.description: Version of the container format as written in the file, if any.

images.description: Images in the file (empty for tables, spectra and traces).

images_total.description:
Set when `images` lists only the first few images ([`InfoOutput::cap_images`]: screening
plates by default, whose field images are all alike, or `--max-images N`): how many
images the file holds. `plate.wells[].images` still indexes every field, the image
commands take any index, and `--max-images 0` (MCP `max_images: 0`) lists them all.

notes.description: Notes the reader wants the caller to see (e.g. "pyramid levels skipped").

path.description: The path as given by the caller.

plate.description:
Multi-well plates (high-content screening): the plate id and type, rows and columns,
the imaged wells with the images (fields) of each, and how many planes the copy on disk
is missing (`docs/formats/hcs.md`). Absent for other files.

size_bytes.description: Size in bytes (for directory formats such as Bruker `.d`, the files that were read).

spectra.description: Mass-spectrometry runs. Empty for other formats.

tables.description: Tabular datasets (flow cytometry events, ...). Empty for image formats.

traces.description: Sampled-signal blocks (electrophysiology, chromatography, NMR). Empty for other formats.

InstrumentInfo.description: The instrument and software that produced the file.

model.description: Instrument model (e.g. microscope stand or mass spectrometer).

acquisition.description:
Present when the file is not finished: still being written (`in_progress`) or
stopped before the end (`interrupted`). See `book/src/guides/lab-shares.md`.

entries_total.description: How many elements of each kind the container holds, when `entries` lists only some.

format.description: Format id of the input file.

notes.description: What was left out of `entries` and how to list it.

LsEntry.description: One row of `info --view structure`: a structural element of the container.

image.description: Which image this element belongs to, if any.

name.description: Element name (an id, a chunk name or a path inside the container).

offset.description: Byte offset of the element in the file, when it has one.

size.description: Size of the element in bytes, when known.

Measurement.description: One thing that was measured, in scientific words.

indices.description: Indices into that array (images, tables, traces or runs) this entry covers.

kind.description: Which array of the file it describes.

technique.description: The technique (CHMO, FBbi, OBI or PSI-MS term).

terms.description: Further terms: polarity, spectrum types, detectors, acquisition modes.

what.description:
What was measured, e.g. `fluorescence, 3 channels (DAPI, GFP, mCherry), 21 z-slices` or
`LC-MS, negative mode, 2,031 scans, MS1`.

MeasurementKind.description: Which part of the file a measurement describes.

oneOf.description: `images[]`.
`tables[]`.
`traces[]`.
`spectra[]`.

name.description: Name of the acquisition method, protocol or experiment as the software saved it.

parameters.description: Method settings, keyed by our own snake_case names (`nucleus`, `polarity`, `z_step`).

technique.description: The technique (CHMO, FBbi or OBI term: `liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry`, ...).

stitched_on_read.description: Whether the reader stitches tiles into a single plane on read.

tile_count.description: Number of tiles (fields of view) in the mosaic.

tile_height.description: Height of one tile in pixels, when all tiles share it.

tile_width.description: Width of one tile in pixels, when all tiles share it.

immersion.description: Immersion medium between lens and sample (`Oil`, `Water`, `Air`, ...).

model.description: Objective model name as the vendor records it.

Origin.description: Where one experiment value came from.

from.description:
The field it was taken from: a path into the `info` JSON (`spectra[0].extra.vial`), or a
vendor file inside the dataset (`pdata/1/title`).

source.description:
How the meaning of the source field is known (the reader's provenance for that field;
`inferred` for our own mapping and derived text).

PhysicalSize.description: Physical pixel size in micrometres (the OME default unit). Every present value is > 0.

x.description: Pixel width in µm (the distance between neighbouring columns).

y.description: Pixel height in µm (the distance between neighbouring rows).

z.description: Spacing between Z planes (focal slices) in µm.

PixelType.description: Sample type of one channel value. Names follow OME-XML `PixelType` values.

oneOf.description: Signed 8-bit integer.
Signed 16-bit integer.
Signed 32-bit integer.
Unsigned 8-bit integer.
Unsigned 16-bit integer (the usual microscope camera output).
Unsigned 32-bit integer.
32-bit IEEE 754 floating point.
64-bit IEEE 754 floating point.
Signed 64-bit integer.
Unsigned 64-bit integer.
Complex number of two 32-bit floats (real, then imaginary): OME `complex`.
Complex number of two 64-bit floats (real, then imaginary): OME `double-complex`.

PlateSummary.description: Layout of a multi-well plate (high-content screening): `info` → `plate`.

columns.description: Number of columns of the plate (12 for a 96-well plate).

complete.description: True when every plane the index names is on disk.

extra.description: Format-specific plate facts in the reader's documented vocabulary.

field_count.description: Most fields of view in one well.

id.description: Plate identifier or barcode as the acquisition software recorded it.

name.description: Plate name, when recorded besides the id.

planes_absent.description:
Planes the instrument never acquired or recorded (they read as blank and are left out
of statistics; `images[].extra.absent_planes`).

planes_expected.description: Planes the plate's index lists (every image's `plane_count`).

planes_missing.description: Planes whose files the index names but that are not on disk (`check` lists them).

plate_type.description: Plate type (product) as recorded, e.g. `384 PerkinElmer CellCarrier Ultra`.

rows.description: Number of rows of the plate (8 for a 96-well plate).

wells.description: The imaged wells, row by row.

PlateWell.description: One imaged well of a plate.

images.description: Indices of the images (fields of view) of this well, in field order.

planes_missing.description: Planes of this well whose files are not on disk (0 when the well is complete).

well.description: Well name, e.g. `C05` (row letters, column zero-padded to two digits).

Quantity.description: A value with an optional unit: `{"value": 19, "unit": "min", "ucum": "min"}`.

unit.description: Unit as written for people (`µm`, `°C`), when the value has one.

value.description: A number, a string, or a list of them.

ResolutionLevel.description: Geometry of one resolution level of an image.

downsample_x.description: Level-0 width over this level's width (1 for level 0; 2, 4, ... for a halving pyramid).

downsample_y.description: Level-0 height over this level's height.

level.description: Level index: 0 is full resolution, larger is more downsampled (`--level`).

size_z.description:
Number of z planes at this level, when it differs from the image's `size_z` (Imaris
downsamples z as well).

tile_width.description:
Width of the tiles (subblocks, chunks) the level is stored in, when it is tiled: region
reads aligned to this grid decode each tile once.

Sample.description: What was measured: the sample's identity as the file records it.

id.description: The sample's identifier, from the field named in `source_field`.

name.description: A descriptive sample name when the file records one besides the id.

sequence_position.description: Position in the autosampler sequence or tray (vial `D:35`, `2:A,8`).

source_field.description:
Path of the field `id` came from (`spectra[0].extra.sample_name`, `tables[0].extra.specimen`,
`pdata/1/title`).

Scope.description: Which outputs of a file a feature, a structure or a calibration affects.

oneOf.description: The normalized metadata (`info`, all its views): sizes, channels, instrument, times.
Image planes (`planes`, `stats`, `export` of images, `preview`).
Mass spectra and scan headers (`scans`, `spectrum`, `analyze chromatogram`, mzML export).
Sampled signals (`trace`, electrophysiology, chromatograms, NMR and IR/Raman spectra).
Tables (FCS events, plate reads, qPCR results, event and peak tables).

SignalChannelInfo.description: One channel of a sampled-signal dataset.

dtype.description: NumPy-style dtype of the raw stored samples.

extra.description: Format-specific channel metadata in the reader's documented vocabulary.

scale.description: `value = raw * scale + offset` when the file stores integers.

unit.description: Physical unit of the scaled values (`pA`, `mV`, `AU`, ...).

Source.description: How we learned what a field means. Ordered from most to least authoritative.

oneOf.description: A published specification or open standard (e.g. OME-XML, FCS 3.1).
The vendor's own published implementation or documentation (e.g. ZEISS libCZI docs).
Permissively licensed community readers whose documentation is public (czifile, liffile, nd2).
Our own differential analysis of files in the corpus.

SpectraInfo.description: A collection of mass spectra (one acquisition run).

extra.description: Format-specific run metadata in the reader's documented vocabulary.

ms_levels.description: MS levels present (1 = full scans, 2 = MS/MS, ...).

name.description: Run name, if the file records one.

scan_count.description: Number of spectra (scans) in the run.

TableInfo.description: A tabular dataset inside the file (rows × columns), e.g. FCS events.

extra.description: Format-specific table metadata in the reader's documented vocabulary.

name.description: Table name, if the format has one.

Term.description: An ontology term: its id (CURIE, e.g. `CHMO:0000524`) and label.

label.description: The term's label in its ontology (`positive scan`).

TraceInfo.description: A block of uniformly sampled signals (a sweep, a chromatogram run, an FID).

extra.description: Format-specific trace metadata in the reader's documented vocabulary.

name.description: Trace name, if the format has one.

sample_count.description: Samples per sweep (the longest sweep when sweeps differ; see `extra.sweep_sample_counts`).

start_s.description: Time of the first sample relative to the recording start, seconds.

sweep_count.description: Number of sweeps/episodes stored back to back (1 for continuous recordings).

Undecoded.description: A structure the reader met in the file but did not decode.

detail.description: What is known about it and what the reader does instead.

scope.description:
Outputs that may be incomplete or wrong because of it. Empty: it is left out and the
values returned do not depend on it.

structure.description: What the structure is, in the format notes' vocabulary.

VariantFeature.description: One feature of the file's fingerprint, with the corpus evidence for it.

corpus_files.description: Development-corpus files with this value confirmed by an independent reader.

scope.description: Outputs whose decoding depends on it (empty: descriptive only).

Withheld.description:
A field `--strict` withholds: it is present, but its value was assumed, derived by a rule no
independent reader confirmed, or never compared with an independent reader.

field.description: JSON path pattern in `info` (`[]` matches any index).
